source.title: RSTeller: Scaling Up Visual Language Modeling in Remote Sensing with Rich Linguistic Semantics from Openly Available Data and Large Language Models
source.authors: Junyao Ge; Xu Zhang; Yang Zheng; Kai-Tai Guo; Ji-Min Liang

record.file_problem: The article text is present through its conclusion, references, and appendix. Some extracted figure text is garbled, but the study is identifiable and its main sections are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether increasing remote-sensing training-data scale changes downstream VLM performance, using continual pre-training and downstream classification and retrieval error rather than held-out language-model cross-entropy.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling-law work but does not measure language-model held-out loss, parameter/token/compute scaling laws, or compute-optimal allocations. The relevant original results are its own downstream performance trends as remote-sensing data scale increases. Baseline checkpoint results and individual benchmark results are included where they report trends or slopes; comparisons cited from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: Section 4.5 trains CLIP ViT-B/32 and ViT-L/14 (WIT checkpoints) on 25/50/75/100% of ~5.2M remote-sensing pairs. It fits linear trends to zero-shot classification and retrieval error. This is a new setting (continual pre-training of VLMs, domain-data scale) with a downstream-vs-scale result bearing on V6. No loss, power-law, compute or allocation analysis is done, so T3 fits better than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that more RS domain data generally improves zero-shot classification and retrieval, with benchmark-dependent gains, initial degradation on some benchmarks and an RSI-CB anomaly. They recommend continued data scaling and larger models. They fit linear trends to downstream error, not power laws to loss.
record.recipe_differences: The original claim concerns held-out language-model loss and compute/parameter/token scaling. This study continually pre-trains CLIP VLMs on increasing amounts of remote-sensing image-text data and fits linear trends to downstream task error.
record.method_sensitivity: The data-scale trend varies across benchmark datasets; RSI-CB reverses for ViT-L/14, and Million-AID is nearly flat for ViT-B/32. The paper also notes initial degradation on some benchmarks before further data scaling improves performance.
record.peer_reviewed: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
record.problems: The scaling experiment uses four data-scale increments and linear fits rather than testing a power-law loss relation. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the fitted slopes. Results vary across benchmarks, and the authors note an unexpected reversal for RSI-CB with ViT-L/14.
record.rows_left_out: Individual plotted performance values and benchmark-specific slopes not discussed numerically in the text were not extracted; see Figs. 11–12. The retained rows cover the aggregate trends and explicitly discussed benchmark-specific exceptions.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss, and no scaling in parameters, tokens or compute.
No fit on small runs extrapolated to larger ones; only four data points spanning less than one order of magnitude.
No fixed-compute allocation of parameters vs data.
No shape variation at fixed parameter count.
Continual pre-training of image-text models, but no power-law form is fitted (linear fits to error) and no loss is reported.

Untested parts: downstream performance vs pretraining loss, and vs model size (only two models, differing in patch size and depth, compared qualitatively). Predictive accuracy is also untested: there is no held-out prediction and no uncertainty on slopes. Scale here is domain data in continual pre-training, not pretraining scale.
No comparison of fitting choices or curvature analysis.

missing.what: RESISC with ViT-L/14: initial degradation then steady decline, k = −0.89
AID with ViT-L/14: degrades when domain data is introduced and never surpasses the baseline checkpoint even at 100% data
ViT-L/14 outperforms ViT-B/32 on most benchmarks, before and after fine-tuning (qualitative model-size comparison)
Other per-benchmark slopes (AID, fMoW for both models; retrieval per-benchmark slopes) shown only in garbled figure text

record.verdict_notes: This is primarily a dataset paper; the scaling result is one experiment with four data scales, two models, one initial checkpoint (WIT) and no error bars. The x-axis spans only ~4x, so claims of predictability are weak. Rows otherwise match the text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Does not fit loss laws on small runs or test loss predictions on larger runs.
Does not compare parameter/token allocations at fixed compute or estimate compute-optimal scaling.
Does not isolate architecture details at a fixed parameter count.
Uses image-text VLMs, but does not test whether a power-law loss form holds in other modalities or training regimes.
Tests downstream classification and retrieval performance against domain-data scale, not performance against model size or pretraining loss.
Does not compare fitting choices for scaling laws or examine whether loss curves depart from power laws.

conditions.value: approximately 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100% of about 5.2 million image-text pairs

rows.measure: Slope k of top-1 classification error versus domain data used (in millions)
rows.note: The authors report a generally improving average trend as domain data scale increases.
rows.check: Value correct (kAverage = −0.50, ViT-B/32). The baseline is the un-fine-tuned WIT checkpoint (stars in Fig. 11), not 'not stated'. It is unclear whether that point enters the fit.

relationships.condition: Average zero-shot classification (both models), retrieval for ViT-L/14, and benchmarks PatternNet/RESISC (ViT-B/32) and EuroSAT (ViT-L/14), as RS domain data grows from ~1.3M to ~5.2M pairs
relationships.reason: Negative error slopes: r1 −0.50, r2 −0.63, r9 −0.84, r3 −1.14, r4 −0.64, r5 −1.50. These come from linear fits on four points with no uncertainty.
relationships.display_finding: Fitted error slopes were −0.50, −0.63, −0.84, −1.14, −0.64, and −1.50 across the specified evaluations, based on four data sizes without uncertainty estimates.

relationships.condition: ViT-B/32 retrieval; ViT-L/14 AID and RESISC early in scaling
relationships.reason: ViT-B/32 retrieval improves only weakly (r8, −0.17). Text reports initial degradation for AID/RESISC on ViT-L/14, and AID never beats the baseline even at full data (not in rows).
relationships.display_finding: ViT-B/32 retrieval improved weakly, with a reported value of −0.17, while ViT-L/14 initially degraded on AID and RESISC and never exceeded the AID baseline.

relationships.condition: RSI-CB with ViT-L/14; Million-AID with ViT-B/32
relationships.reason: Error rises with more domain data for RSI-CB (r6, k = +0.90) and is flat for Million-AID (r7, k = −0.00).
relationships.display_finding: Error increased for RSI-CB with k=+0.90 and remained flat for Million-AID with k=−0.00.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Average zero-shot classification and retrieval results for the tested ViT-B/32 and ViT-L/14 models as remote-sensing training data increases
reader_labels.reason: The reported average error slopes are negative for both models and both task families, indicating generally improving downstream performance with more domain data (r1, r2, r8, r9).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Individual classification benchmarks, including Million-AID and RSI-CB
reader_labels.reason: The trend is not uniform across benchmarks: the ViT-B/32 Million-AID slope is effectively zero, while ViT-L/14 RSI-CB error rises with more data (r6, r7).
